question.text: Satpura Fund-I (Cat II) has completed final distributions and the fund is being wound up. The Manager is asked about the post-winding-up record retention period. Per SEBI (AIF) Regulations, for how long must records such as AUM, valuation policies, investment strategies, investor details, capital contributions and investment decision-making process be maintained?

answer.text: Perpetual retention is required; records can never be destroyed

explanation.text: The Logic: Per SEBI (AIF) Regulations, the Sponsor and/or Manager of the AIF is required to maintain, for a period of 5 YEARS AFTER the winding up of the fund, records such as: assets under the scheme/fund, valuation policies and practices, investment strategies, details of investors and their capital contribution, and investment decision-making process. This supports SEBI's inspection rights and investor grievance redressal even post-wind-up. The Trap: 1-year and 3-year options understate. The perpetual-retention option overstates (no perpetual-retention rule exists; 5 years is the fixed post-wind-up window). Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the same 5-year rule. XXIV (AML) tests 5-year KYC retention (same number, different regulation — PMLA). III-A/III-C covers record-retention across SEBI intermediaries. Manager's Pro-Tip: Migrate records to a secure digital archive BEFORE wind-up dissolves the operating entity. Name a custodian-of-records (often a group-company or empanelled law firm) for the 5-year window and document chain-of-custody. Failure here can trigger SEBI adjudication years after wind-up.
